title: Nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to quantum reservoirs
abstract: A statistical mechanical formulation where nonequilibrium averages of selected quantum observables are given exactly as averages over local density operators is used to describe the dynamics and thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to reservoirs. The local density operators are functionals of constraint variables that play the role of thermodynamic forces that satisfy a set of equations of motion. A focus of the work is on the evolution of the average internal energy of the quantum subsystem that may be subject to external autonomous driving that does work on the system, and on entropy production in the system. The nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics the quantum subsystem coupled to reservoirs, as well as that for the isolated subsystem and reservoirs, are discussed. When the subsystem is coupled to large quantum reservoirs, the effects of the quantum subsystem on the reservoirs can be captured through boundary conditions on the reservoir equations, and these boundary conditions are derived. The formulation is illustrated by considering the heat transfer through a system comprising a quantum system coupled to two heat reservoirs with different temperatures.
summary: This paper develops a generalized statistical mechanical framework to study the non-equilibrium thermodynamics of a small quantum system interacting with large quantum reservoirs. It utilizes a local density operator formalism, constrained by measured average observables, to derive exact equations of motion for key quantities like internal energy and entropy production. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for analyzing energy and entropy flow in driven quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical description of non-equilibrium dynamics and thermodynamics for a small quantum system coupled to large quantum reservoirs.
main_result: It derives exact evolution equations for internal energy and entropy production using a local density operator formalism constrained by thermodynamic forces.
method: The core method involves constructing a local density operator by maximizing an entropy functional subject to constraints derived from the system's average observables.
model_or_system: The model consists of a small quantum subsystem coupled to large quantum reservoirs, described by a total Hamiltonian $H(\lambda t) = H_S(\lambda t) + V_c + H_R$. The dynamics are governed by the Liouville equation.
key_observables: Average internal energy, entropy production ($\sigma(t)$), work ($W(t)$), and the local density operators ($\hat{ho}_L(t)$).
important_parameters: External driving protocols ($\lambda t$), reservoir temperatures, and the set of constrained observables $\{A(r)\}$.
main_assumptions: The formalism assumes that the effects of the subsystem on the reservoirs can be captured via boundary conditions, and certain mode-coupling corrections are neglected.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by first defining the local density operator via entropy maximization, then deriving the evolution equations for average fields and energy, and finally presenting appendices detailing the calculation of projected evolution operators and constraint variable dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, general framework for calculating non-equilibrium quantities like entropy production and energy flow in open quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding quantum thermal machines and energy conversion processes.
